items.title: Magnarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: I transcribed Coltrane’s second solo... I transcribed that one... he has devices that he plays over and over again... I think that he plays so creatively

ctx.x: It makes, technology seems to me, in my generation, it seems to make things a little too easy or something. Well, time does go by. I was listening to you play today and I’m trying to get a handle on what you think about, if you’re playing a tune like let’s say “Countdown,” it’s pretty darn hard and the tempo is pretty bright. Are the chord changes going by in your head? And are you trying to choose notes from them?

Well in “Countdown” [inaudible] I had to play it once with a band. I’ve gone through “Countdown,” I’ve gone through “Satellite.” I like to play “Satellite.” I like to play “Giant Steps,” so I’m familiar with that, but “Countdown” is actually the hardest song I think. It’s more difficult. Because people like to play it like [scats]. I’m singing “Satellite,” but anyway “Countdown” the tempo is like [scats] and the changes move really quick. So yeah, I do think about the changes and I do actually have things worked…
a little stronger because he’s slipping and sliding around and it’s like wow, that’s really beautiful.
